byFamily.title: Warming avoided in {year}, by lever group
byFamily.note: Each group's part is the mean of what it adds over every order the groups could be counted in, so no group is counted first; a group acting on several causes is split between them. The parts add up to the total.

link.headline: By {year} the world has warmed by {total}.
link.scenario: With the levers chosen, the world would be {avoided} cooler in {year} than without them ({ssp}): {parts}.
link.intro: Most warming comes from burning fossil fuels. Farming adds to it in a different way: mostly through methane from cattle and rice paddies, and nitrous oxide from fertiliser and manure, gases that trap far more heat than CO₂ while they last.
link.attributionText: Each band is the warming from one cause, or, below zero, the cooling. After today, each band is what is left once the levers chosen act on its cause; the dashed outlines are the bands without the levers. The line is the temperature measured.
link.attributionCaption: Medians of FaIR runs on historical emissions by sector, then the chosen scenario after today; each cause is the warming its emissions add. Air pollution cools: its particles reflect sunlight and brighten clouds. The energy, heating and industry levers also cut the air pollution of the fuel they no longer burn, so its cooling shrinks when they act.
link.attributionLabel: Stacked chart of warming by cause from {from} to {year}, with observed temperature
link.gasesText: Each gas on its own scale: a tonne of each warms very differently.
link.gasLabel: World farm emissions of {gas} from {from} to {year}
link.whyTitle: Why the gases are kept apart
link.whyMethane: Methane is short-lived: about half of it is gone within twelve years. Emit less of it and the warming it causes starts to fall within decades, which is why a change in what we eat shows up before 2050.
link.whyNitrous: Nitrous oxide lasts about a century, so less of it slows warming steadily rather than reversing it.
link.whyCo2: CO₂ stays for centuries; the warming it has caused stays too. Adding the gases up as CO₂e hides these differences, so Planetshift computes the temperature from each gas separately.
link.parts: What each cause adds or takes away: {parts}.

chart.title: What the chart shows
chart.text: The chart shows global warming since 1850: the observed temperature, then two paths to 2050 or 2100, without the levers and with the levers you set. The shaded band around each path is its likely range. The Warming avoided tab shows the gap between the two.

levers.title: How the levers work
levers.text: The Levers panel lists every lever under the cause of warming it acts on. Open a group and move a slider to set how much of a lever is adopted: the chart, the summary and the map change at once. The figure beside each group is the warming it would avoid alone, in full. Every setting is kept in the page address, so a link reopens it.

causes.title: Where the causes are
causes.text: The Causes of warming tab, above the chart, splits the warming by cause (fossil fuels and industry, farming, land use and the others) and shows what the levers take off each. The Methodology page explains every step and its sources.
